title: Outsourcing and offshoring

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches offshoring, which the new point needs, and both are written at Year 12 depth rather than for Year 8 students, so the card would need a new step and a change of depth rather than small edits.

draft.title: Outsourcing and offshoring
card: a business pays another business to do some of its work, such as payroll or cleaning. The other business can be in Australia or overseas.
a business moves some of its work to another country. It is often done because wages there are lower.
The two ideas are different. Work can be outsourced within Australia, and a business can offshore work to its own overseas branch.
Businesses may do either to cut costs. Australian workers can lose jobs when the work moves, though new jobs may appear elsewhere.
draft.remember: Outsourcing is about who does the work. Offshoring is about where the work is done.

a.q: A Perth company pays a Perth cleaning firm to clean its offices. What is this?
opts: Outsourcing, because another business does the work
Offshoring, because another business does the work
Offshoring, because the work is done by a cleaner
Outsourcing, because the work is done in Australia
a.why: The company pays a separate business to do work it once did itself, which is outsourcing. It is not offshoring, because the work stays in Australia and nothing moves overseas.
a.clue: Was the work moved to another country?

b.q: Tane's Hobart software firm closes its help desk in Hobart and opens a new help desk in its own office in Manila, where wages are lower. What is this?
opts: Offshoring, because the work moved to another country
Outsourcing, because the work moved to a new help desk
Outsourcing, because the work now costs less to do
Offshoring, because the firm stopped doing the work
b.why: The work moved to another country where wages are lower, so it is offshoring. It is not outsourcing, because the firm still does the work itself in its own office and pays no other business.
b.clue: Is another business being paid to do the work?

a.best: Outsourcing, because another business does the work

b.best: Offshoring, because the work moved to another country

problems.detail: Why (a) says the company pays a firm to do work 'it once did itself', but the question never says the company did its own cleaning before. This could suggest that outsourcing only counts when a business hands over work it used to do. The card only says a business pays another business to do some of its work.

check.summary: The card, remember line, questions and options are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The only issue is that why (a) adds a detail not in the question: that the company once did the cleaning itself.
